title: Adaptive queue fidelity shaper with admission control and graceful degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an admission-and-queue shaping subsystem (the 'fidelity shaper') that dynamically adjusts request fidelity and queuing priority across tenants during overload and region failover. This ticket covers design, prototype, integration with circuit breakers, SLO mappings, metrics, and a staged rollout plan.

Background: Current overload handling uses static priority lanes and simple token buckets. We need a more expressive, tenant-aware mechanism that: (1) preserves high-value customer SLOs, (2) gracefully degrades non-critical requests (e.g., lower sampling, compressed responses, model-slimming fallbacks), and (3) coordinates across multi-region failover so the system does not amplify load during failover window.

Scope:
- Admission controller that enforces per-tenant budgets and global capacity while exposing soft-fail modes (degrade vs reject).
- Priority bands with dynamic fidelity rules: each band maps to a degradation policy (truncate context, switch to smaller model, compress output, reduce streaming chunks).
- Eviction-aware queue shaping: when KV cache/worker memory is constrained, the shaper reduces queue depth for low-priority bands and increases preemptive eviction budgets.
- Circuit breaker integration: closed/open/half-open states drive admission aggressiveness; open circuits trigger conservative fidelity policies.
- Multi-region coordination: a small telemetry-based leader election so the region in failover mode can be proactively throttled instead of failing over every request.
- Observability: SLO dashboards, per-tenant drop/reject rates, fidelity transition counts, and synthetic health probes.

Design notes / decisions:
- Policy model: JSON policy objects per-tenant (server-side managed) with immutable versioned releases. Policies include priority weight, budget window (tokens), fidelity ladder (ordered degradations), and circuit thresholds. Policies are applied at admission time; a subsequent runtime layer enforces fidelity changes.
- Degradation primitives: defined as discrete actions rather than free-form code to make metrics and rollbacks safe. Examples: "model-variant=small", "truncate-prefix=256", "response-compression=aggressive", "sampling=0.5".
- Backpressure vs rejection: prefer soft degradation when predicted downstream latency is < 2x SLO; otherwise hard reject with clear retry-after headers for idempotent routes.
- Predictive hints: admission controller will optionally consume latency forecasts from the predictive-shedding service (ENG-221007) if available.

Trade-offs:
- Complexity vs predictability: policy model adds complexity for operators but enables precise SLO prioritization; to mitigate, we will ship a small default policy set and an opinionated policy generator.
- State burden: per-tenant budgets increase memory/coord state. We'll use an LRU cache and best-effort persistence; tenants without persistent budget will use conservative defaults.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype: local in-runtime admission module + simulator to replay production traces (2 weeks).
2) Integration: hook into runtime route matching, expose metrics, add policy APIs to control plane (3 weeks).
3) Canary: rollout to internal tenants and low-traffic customers with telemetry and automated rollback (2 weeks).
4) Gradual expansion: enable predictive hints and multi-region coordination logic (2 weeks).

Acceptance criteria:
- SLO: maintain 99th percentile p99 latency for priority band A under 75% of current peak load, and keep degradation for lower bands visible but bounded.
- Observability: dashboards show per-tenant fidelity transitions and per-route reject rates; alerts for fidelity-flapping.
- Safety: automatic rollback path if errors >= 5% in 5m.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (internal drive): https://drive.internal.redwood/designs/adaptive-fidelity-shaper (linked PRD pending).
- Simulator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fidelity-sim (prototype branch).
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421 (WIP).

Next steps: finish prototype simulator, iterate policy schema, schedule cross-team review with Console/PM/SE for rollout controls, and request security review for policy APIs.
